x-m-el-job-02.title: Saying the Same Speed Using Two Units

x-m-el-job-02.material: Two running-club members describe same speed with different units. One say 'x m per minute' (distance cover in 1 minute), the other say 'y km per hour' (distance cover in 1 hour). Dem want state the numbers as natural numbers only, no decimals or fractions.

x-m-el-job-02.s.s2.fail.c2: x m per minute and y km per hour no be same speed. Compare distance for 1 hour with same unit.

x-m-el-job-02.s.s2.fail.c3: The speed per hour must be from 6 to 20 inclusive.
x-m-el-job-02.s.s2.explain: 100 m per minute na 6000 m in 1 hour, so na 6 km per hour. Each time speed per minute increase by 50 m, speed per hour increase by 3 km. So possible pairs na 100/6, 150/9, 200/12, 250/15, 300/18.
x-m-el-job-02.s.s2.because.prompt: Explain why 7 km or 8 km per hour no work, but 6, 9, and 12 km work.

x-m-el-job-02.s.s2.because.placeholder: Example: If you change speed per hour to speed per minute, ...

x-m-el-job-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You explain why the rule use 3 (or 50) specifically?
x-m-el-job-02.s.s2.because.model.0: y km per hour changed to speed per minute na 1000×y÷60 = 50y/3 m. For answer to be natural number, y must multiple of 3, so 6, 9, 12 work, and 7, 8 no work.
x-m-el-job-02.s.s2.because.model.1: x m per minute na 60x m = 0.06x km in 1 hour. For both to be whole numbers, x must multiple of 50; then hourly speed go increase by 3 each time.
x-m-el-job-02.s.s2.because.model.2: Changing y km per hour to per-minute speed give 50y/3, so y must divide by 3 to be natural number. 6, 9, 12 work, 7 and 8 no work.

At festival stage, clubs A, B, C, and D perform once each, one after another. Conditions be these.
① A no fit perform first because of equipment setup.
② D no fit perform last because of another commitment.
③ B video na background for C performance, so B must perform before C.

x-m-el-job-05.s.s1.explain: All 24 orders for 4 clubs pair up if you swap B and C before/after positions. Exactly half, 12 ways, follow condition ③.

x-m-el-job-05.s.s2.fail.c5: B must perform before C (condition ③).

x-m-el-job-05.s.s2.because.prompt: Find how many possible orders there are altogether and write the method wey make you sure say you miss none.

x-m-el-job-05.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You check say your counting no count the same order twice?

x-m-el-job-06.title: Fixing a Solution for Counting Activity Schedules
x-m-el-job-06.goal: Separate cases where order matter from cases where e no matter, find and fix mistake in solution counting activity schedules, and check with another method.
x-m-el-job-06.material: On field trip day, choose 3 from 5 activities (A, B, C, D, E) and assign one to morning, afternoon, and evening slots. Activity A dey outdoors, so dem no fit do am evening. Student solve how many possible assignments there be.

x-m-el-job-06.s.s2.model.0: Morning and afternoon get order, so no divide by 2; e na 4×3 = 12. So 60 − 12 = 48.

x-m-el-job-03.title: Judging the Actual Area of a Room from Scale Drawing

x-m-el-job-07.title: Comparing Paint Amount Estimates
x-m-el-job-07.topic: Validity of cost and material calculations
x-m-el-job-07.goal: See why different estimates give same conclusion, then find conditions yourself where estimate safe and where conclusion change.
x-m-el-job-07.material:
You wan paint only four walls of room wey long 4 m, wide 3 m and high 2.5 m, twice (2 coats). Windows and door total area na 3.2 square meters, no paint dem. 1 L paint cover 10 square meters for one coat, sold only in 4 L cans. Four people estimate how many cans needed with different methods.
A: Floor na 4×3 = 12 square meters, so paint 12 square meters twice na 24 square meters, 2.4 L, so 1 can.
B: Wall area 35 square meters minus 3.2 na 31.8; two coats na 63.6 square meters, 6.36 L, so 2 cans.
C: Ignore windows and door; painting 35 square meters twice na 70 square meters, 7 L, so 2 cans.
D: Paint 31.8 square meters once na 3.18 L, so 1 can.
